title: Lit Screen, Lit Eyes
subtitle: An empty heart and a pair of longing eyes.

trails.title: Syncing Up
trails.description: Welcome to the Arcade Restaurant. May I take your order?

content.text: My dear child, look at you, you're exhausted. I couldn't be of help then, but it's ok, the "party" is over now. At least let me brush your hair, darling.
Or your hair will get all knotted, and it will hurt you when you try to untangle them.
Indeed. It happened more than once.

branch.text: I'm not surprised. An old friend of ours, "knot." Often we learn our knots before we even know how to read and write.
A knot could be an obstacle that breaks the consistency of a flow, and also a reminder of forgotten things.
You can use just about anything on hand to make a knot: leaves of grass, the fur of an animal, even fallen hair ... But the sturdiest knots are tied with rope.
Knots are to be found in many stories. Signify promises, counting and measuring, an instrument of salvation and one of execution.

content.text: What else can these knots really do?

branch.text: Oh, I could go on all day! The influence and power of knots can't be overstated...

It is said that it was in the cutting of the Gordian Knot that Alexander became "the Great"; just touching the meters-long rope provides blessings to the faithful in Belem; and tiny knots on strings can carry the history of an entire people.

The ancient Inca called it "Quipu." The intricate variations of hundreds of fabrics, colors, and lengths of strings were used to record their stories through the ages. And to think, Shakespeare only had 26 letters to create his masterpieces.

content.text: Isn't there something a bit more practical?

branch.text: Just look around you: don't sailors use knots to mark depths and mend sails; or coachmen tying knots to rein their horses; and any respectable lady or gentleman knows the knots they must tie about their necks to stay in fashion.
Or consider the knot-like helix structure of DNA, and the changes in states of matter ... Invisible to the naked eye, these knots carry some hint at a universal law.
That there might be a string, like the Quipu, an endless rope that records in its knots everything in the world. One that can't be seen, yet there it is, everywhere, all at once.
Maybe you can tie this knot yourself. Use your hair, then form a loop, pass the end through it, and tighten it up. There you go.
I hope you keep this knot as a record of the words we shared here.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: The hell?! I thought movie stars were just empty suits.
Another volley of silver needles streaks through the air, forcing Liáng and Poitier back.
Qí Xīng stands at the center of the alley. Though seemingly trapped between Liáng and Poitier, she skillfully uses their positioning to her advantage.
Neither officer can risk injuring the other by firing their gun or using an arcane skill, leaving the battle at a deadlock.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: We're not going to last much longer. I have to do something. Poitier, cover me.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Arise Qiángliáng, swift and fierce!
With the ritual vessel of Qiángliáng in her hand, Liáng recites the ancient incantation, each syllable clear and deliberate.
Qí Xīng looks momentarily stunned.
This is the beginning of an incantation. Liáng knows that more silver needles could come flying at her at any moment.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Banish all evil ...
For a brief moment, hesitation creeps over her.
As a child, she sat before the screen and watched this figure over and over again, her eyes filled with admiration. She had mimicked her arcane skill countless times.
But she never imagined that, one day, those dazzling silver needles would be aimed at her.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: ... and cleanse this place!
Yet, she still speaks the final words of the incantation.
With these words, an ancient contract will be upheld, and the Xiǎndào Beast will be called upon to devour all evil. As is her right as a descendant of the Liáng family.
At least, that's what's supposed to happen.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: What?
But the alley remains as empty as it was before.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: Hey!

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Rookie, watch out!
Someone pushes her aside. She hits the ground hard. A flash of silver. The sound of shouting.
Then, blood. A body falling. A sticky sensation. Warmth. Chaos ...
The events that follow are hazy in Liáng's memory.

items.speaker: Enraged Man
items.text: Training isn't over! Stand firm!
A sharp reprimand shatters her haze, pulling her back to focus.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: That's ...
A familiar courtyard. A man with a familiar face.
In front of him, a little girl stands in horse stance, sweat rolling down her forehead. Her legs are trembling.
Yet, the man's ebony ruler comes down mercilessly on the girl's shoulder.

items.speaker: Enraged Man
items.text: Wrong! Shoulders and elbows down! Relax your body and mind. How many times do I have to repeat myself?
Two small heads peek over the courtyard wall, giggling and whispering to each other.

items.speaker: Boy
items.text: Shh. Look, she's gonna fall any second.

items.speaker: Girl
items.text: Heh heh, that's what she gets for saying that to the teacher.
The boy makes a goofy face at the girl holding the stance. The girl, already exhausted, finally loses her balance and collapses to the ground.

items.speaker: Enraged Man
items.text: You don't come to training, you're distracted, and you're lazy. How could Qiángliáng obey such an undisciplined master?

items.speaker: Enraged Man
items.text: Get up. I'll come back later. If you can't do it by sundown, there will be no dinner tonight.
The man, her father, shakes his head in disappointment and walks away, leaving the girl gasping for breath on the ground.

items.speaker: Girl
items.text: Let's go. She's gonna be there all day. Wanna go to the theater?

items.speaker: Boy
items.text: Sure! The one on the corner's playing Detective C07 today.
The children hop down from the wall, laughing as they scurry off.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: The theater? I want to go, too.
No one hears her voice.
No one but herself.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I remember it now. I hated Qiángliáng when I was little.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Father was always trying to teach me something, about the Twelve Zhènzǐ, the Master of Qiángliáng, fighting the wicked and dispelling evil, fulfilling the duty of my inheritance. I was only a child. It was all too difficult for me to understand.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: The other kids hated me. I was a traitor, a class president who took the side of the adults and enforced the rules. They'd all hang out and have fun together while I was left alone. I envied them.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Their lives were simple. I wanted that.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: One cent, two cents ... five ...
Her piggy bank lies smashed on the ground as she picks through the shards to count every coin.
Amidst the broken porcelain, half of a shattered face stares up at her innocently.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I'm sorry, Piggy.
She gently brushes her fingers over its face in a gesture of comfort—or farewell.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: That day, I disobeyed Father, gathered up all my savings, and headed to the theater.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: That was the first time I watched Detective C07. It was amazing.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: But I knew. It was just fiction. Just an escape.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: It wouldn't change anything in my real life. Once the movie was over, I'd have to go back to the same home I had just left.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I didn't want to leave, so I stayed in my seat for the closing credits.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: But the lights didn't come on when the credits ended. Rather, the silver screen lit up again and played something.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: It was an interview with Ms. Qí Xīng.

items.speaker: Reporter
items.text: Ms. Qí Xīng, many children love your work and see you as their hero.

items.speaker: Reporter
items.text: Yet some adults say that the story of Detective C07 is too unrealistic because she always beats the villain.

items.speaker: Reporter
items.text: What's your opinion on this subject? Is it a flaw of the movie?

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: The real world's already a cruel and unfair place. Our movie's idealistic, yes, but it shows us a world where good is rewarded and evil is punished. We need that.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: If we can't accept justice and truth even in a fictional world, then what hope do we have for reality?
Qí Xīng gazes into the camera, but also beyond it, her smile carefree, her eyes shining even brighter than the stars.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: C07 is justice, a hero who fights evil and cares for the weak. She'll always bring a happy ending, no matter what she's faced with.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: One of our goals with this movie, and with the character, was to inspire and encourage our viewers.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: We know that most people can't become a C07 in the real world. After all, it's an incredibly difficult path to take.

items.speaker: Qi Xing
items.text: But we hope that we can at least inspire people to become heroes in their own lives, to create happy endings for themselves and the people around them.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: It was just a short interview like any other, but I still remember every word she said.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: "As the master of Qiángliáng, you must use your power to fight the wicked and dispel evil. It is your duty to maintain the peace of the world."

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Qiángliáng, the powerful being that had always been a blur to me, suddenly became clear.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I realized that I could be more than just a hero who creates happy endings for herself and the people around her. I could be the hero who creates happy endings for everyone, just like C07.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: She was right. Not everyone can do that, but I could, because I was Yuè of the Liáng family, the master of Qiángliáng. On that day, the burden that had been crushing me suddenly became a blessing.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: So, what went wrong?
The image fades as another silver flash brings her back to reality.
Sirens. An ambulance. Blood. Blood. Endless blood. It seeps through the fabric of her uniform, drenching her hands.
She hears someone shouting.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Stay with me, Poitier. Please!

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Why? Why did you do that?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I-I thought you hated me.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: People always hate me.
Now she can hear clearly, she realizes it's her own voice, hoarse with desperation.
What did Poitier say to her back then?
Blood bubbles from her mouth and nose with each painful breath.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: *cough* You could tell, huh?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: But that's—*cough*—that's in the past. Forget it.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: We just didn't know you yet.
A bloodstained hand weakly pats Liáng's cheek before falling limp.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Poitier?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: No! No!! Please! Poitier!

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Ugh, will you shut up? I'm not dead yet.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Ugh!
A thunderous smack, unbelievable from someone confined to a hospital bed, jerks Liáng awake from her nightmare.
Liáng's head throbs. Dazed, she looks around, taking in the sterile white of the hospital room and the irritated face of her instructor.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: The hell you doing sleeping on my thigh, huh? Ugh, my leg's gone numb. And clean up the drool on your chin.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: What? Ah. I'm sorry.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Just kidding, boo. You're not drooling.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Alright, turn on the TV for me. I was bored out of my mind waiting for you to wake up.
